question.problem:
Given that $g(x,y)=\sqrt{x}\,{e}^{x/y}$ and

$$
\frac{∂g}{∂x}=\frac{(2x+y){e}^{x/y}}{2y\sqrt{x}},\,\frac{∂g}{∂y}=-\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}\,{e}^{x/y}}{{y}^{2}},
$$

find the set of values $(x,y)$ where all partial derivatives of $g$ exist.
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that $g(x,y)=\sqrt{x}\,{e}^{x/y}$ is defined only when $x\ge 0$ and $y\ne 0.$ So, the domain of $g$ is 

$$
{D}_{g}=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,y\ne 0\}.
$$

As for the partial derivatives, we have the following.

- The function ${g}_{x}(x,y)=\frac{(2x+y){e}^{x/y}}{2y\sqrt{x}}$ is defined only when $x>0$ and $y\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${g}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{g}_{x}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,x>0,y\ne 0\}.
$$

- The function ${g}_{y}(x,y)=-\frac{\sqrt{{x}^{3}}{e}^{x/y}}{{y}^{2}}$ is defined only when $x\ge 0$ and $y\ne 0.$ So, the domain of ${g}_{x}$ is 

$$
{D}_{{g}_{y}}=\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,y\ne 0\}.
$$

Finally, we conclude that the partials of $g$ exist on the set

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{g}\cap {D}_{{g}_{x}}\cap {D}_{{g}_{y}} & =\{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,y\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y)\,:\,x>0,y\ne 0\}\cap \{(x,y)\,:\,x\ge 0,y\ne 0\} \\  & =\{(x,y)\,:\,x>0,y\ne 0\}.\end{aligned}
$$
